new_edges_required.node1_text: אֲמִירַת תּוֹרָה לְמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְשֵׂכֶל הַמְקַבֵּל
new_edges_required.source_quote: כִּי צָרִיךְ לִזָּהֵר מְאֹד, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְשֵׂכֶל הַמְקַבֵּל. כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת נִאוּף, שֶׁמַּשְׁלִיךְ טִפֵּי הַשֵּׂכֶל בַּאֲתָר דְּלָא אִצְטְרִיךְ
new_edges_required.reason: The central, explicit bechina of this Torah. Saying Torah to someone whose intellect cannot receive it IS (הוּא בְּחִינַת) an act of niuf — adultery/illegitimate seminal emission. The structural logic is: the teacher transmits 'drops of sekhel' (טִפֵּי הַשֵּׂכֶל) to the student's mind, exactly as a man transmits seed. When misdirected, this IS the bechina of casting seed into a place that does not need it ('בַּאֲתָר דְּלָא אִצְטְרִיךְ' — the Aramaic term from Kabbalistic literature for prohibited seed-emission).

new_edges_required.source_quote: וְנִקְרָא לְבַטָּלָה, כִּי אֵינוֹ מוֹלִיד אֶצְלוֹ כְּלוּם
new_edges_required.reason: First variety of niuf: when the transmission produces nothing at all in the recipient, it IS called 'לְבַטָּלָה' (in vain/for nothing). The Talmudic term לְבַטָּלָה for wasted seed is explicitly applied here to the wasted Torah-sekhel. This IS a bechina: the empty/barren misfire IS 'in vain'.

new_edges_required.source_quote: וְלִפְעָמִים נִקְרָא נִאוּף מַמָּשׁ, שֶׁמּוֹלִיד וּמוֹצִיא פָּסוּל וּפָגוּם
new_edges_required.reason: Second variety: when the misdirected Torah-saying DOES produce offspring but that offspring is pasul/pagum (disqualified/flawed — meaning the student acts on the teaching but at the wrong level for his madrega), then it IS called niuf mamash (actual adultery). This distinguishes the barren-misfire case (לְבַטָּלָה) from the corrupted-offspring case (ניאוף ממש).

new_edges_required.source_quote: שֶׁמּוֹלִיד וּמוֹצִיא פָּסוּל וּפָגוּם, הַיְנוּ שֶׁהַמְּקַבֵּל עוֹשֶׂה עַל יְדֵי זֶה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לוֹ לְפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ
new_edges_required.reason: The 'פָּסוּל וּפָגוּם' (disqualified and blemished offspring) is the concrete instantiation of 'ניאוף ממש'. The Rebbe defines it: the recipient does something that is inappropriate to HIS level/madrega. The flawed action IS the bechina of the 'disqualified offspring' of spiritual niuf.

new_edges_required.source_quote: יוּכַל, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו הַיֵּצֶר בְּתַאֲוַת נִאוּף
new_edges_required.reason: The yetzer hara IS specifically manifested as תַּאֲוַת נִאוּף (the desire for adultery/sexual transgression) in this Torah's context. The Rebbe identifies the yetzer's mode of attack on the Torah teacher as precisely this: because the careless teacher has committed spiritual niuf (emitting sekhel-drops inappropriately), the yetzer gains a foothold specifically in the domain of actual sexual desire. The yetzer IS this desire — they share the same essential nature in this Torah.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: This is a metaphorical description within the proof of the bechina, not itself declared as a bechina using בְּחִינַת language. 'שֶׁמַּשְׁלִיךְ טִפֵּי הַשֵּׂכֶל בַּאֲתָר דְּלָא אִצְטְרִיךְ' uses the Zoharic Aramaic phrase to explain WHY the act IS niuf — it is the analogical sub-mechanism, not a separate bechina declaration. Excluded as a standalone node; the concept is implicit in edge 134-B-001.

This is a relational description — the receiver's capacity — used to define the condition under which the niuf-bechina applies. The Rebbe does not say 'שֵׂכֶל הַמְקַבֵּל IS a bechina of X'. It is context-setting language, not a bechina declaration.

Line 3: 'שֶׁדִּבּוּרָיו יִתְחַלְּקוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע כָּל אֶחָד כִּי אִם מַה שֶּׁצָּרִיךְ לוֹ'. This is a practical instruction/eitza derived from the bechina — not itself a bechina statement. The Rebbe is saying: as a result of this principle (eitza), arrange your speech this way. Not a bechina edge.

Line 3-4: The Zohar on Yitro (Shemot 68) and on Tetzaveh (186b) are cited as proof-texts for the practical point about tailored speech. They are not bechina declarations — they are evidential citations. Excluded.
